title.zh: 把不看好的预期拆成一个具体问题
title.en: Turn an unfavourable expectation into a specific question

paragraphs.zh: 回到上面的普通兴趣安排，先用一句话写下自己预期会发生什么，再分别列出已经知道、尚未确认和属于自己感受的部分。例如，“我担心材料准备不齐”可以接着问“清单中哪一项还没确认？”如果并没有具体事件，就留空。复盘的用途是让担忧指向可说明的内容；信息最终也可能支持原来的顾虑，不需要为了离开较低分区而改成积极说法。
paragraphs.en: Return to the ordinary interest arrangement above. State what you expect, then separate known facts, unchecked details and your feelings. “I worry that materials will be missing” might become “Which item on the list remains unconfirmed?” Leave a blank if no particular event comes to mind. The purpose is to make a concern specific. Further information may support it; changing to positive wording is no requirement for leaving a lower reading region.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设一次小活动让人不太看好，最想先确认哪一个具体条件？”先交换具体看法，不需要比较谁更乐观；同一个人也可能对不同事情有不同期待。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If someone expected a small activity to go poorly, which specific condition would they most want confirmed?” Exchange specific views without comparing who is more optimistic. The same person may hold different expectations about different events.

paragraphs.zh: 可以分享这份公开通用说明，链接不含本次答案或分数。对方可以不回答，也不必公开心情、自我感受或私人经历。
paragraphs.en: You can share this public general guide; its link contains no answers or scores from this attempt. The other person may decline and need not disclose mood, self-regard or private experiences.

title.zh: 区分暂未形成期待与已经发现的问题
title.en: Separate an undecided expectation from a known problem

paragraphs.zh: 沿用上面的分享活动，写下目前期待、真正缺少的信息，以及已经确认的限制。三栏可以都有内容，也可以仍然未知。若愿意进一步了解，只挑一项与是否参与有关的条件，例如时间是否合适。没有形成期待和发现明确障碍是两件事；不必把所有未知都记成坏消息，也不用把顾虑改写成热情。最后是否参加，由实际条件和自己的意愿决定。
paragraphs.en: For the sharing activity above, note your present expectation, information still missing and confirmed constraints. Any column may remain unknown. If you want to learn more, choose one condition relevant to participation, such as whether the timing works. An undecided expectation differs from an identified obstacle. Neither treating every unknown as bad news nor rewriting concern as enthusiasm is required. Actual conditions and willingness inform the decision to participate.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设还没决定是否参加兴趣分享，你需要先知道什么，而哪些只是暂时没有判断？”先交换具体看法，不需要比较谁更乐观；同一个人也可能对不同事情有不同期待。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If you had not decided whether to join an interest-sharing session, what would you need to know, and where would you simply have no judgment yet?” Exchange specific views without comparing who is more optimistic. The same person may hold different expectations about different events.

paragraphs.zh: 可以分享这份公开通用说明，链接不含本次答案或分数。对方可以不回答，也不必公开心情、自我感受或私人经历。
paragraphs.en: You can share this public general guide; its link contains no answers or scores from this attempt. The other person may decline and need not disclose mood, self-regard or private experiences.

title.zh: 让不同回答各自保留含义
title.en: Let different responses retain their meaning

paragraphs.zh: 从上面的普通安排里挑一个例子，分别写下看好的部分、担心的部分和暂时不知道的部分。无需让三栏字数相等；它们也不负责解释你每一道题的答案。如果回想起两种不同情境，可以分开记，不用把它们平均成一个态度。这样更容易说明“哪件事、哪一点”，而不是把中段分数当作永远客观的证明。暂时不作结论同样可以。
paragraphs.en: Choose an example from the ordinary arrangement above and note promising details, concerns and unknowns. The columns need no equal length and cannot explain every item response. If two different situations come to mind, keep them separate rather than averaging them into one attitude. This helps specify which aspect of which event you mean, without using a middle total as proof of permanent objectivity. Leaving a conclusion open is also possible.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设对同一次活动有看好的部分，也有不清楚的部分，你会怎样分别说明？”先交换具体看法，不需要比较谁更乐观；同一个人也可能对不同事情有不同期待。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If some parts of an activity seemed promising while others remained unclear, how would you explain them separately?” Exchange specific views without comparing who is more optimistic. The same person may hold different expectations about different events.

title.zh: 给看好的安排补上事实栏
title.en: Add a fact column to a favourable expectation

paragraphs.zh: 沿用上面的普通兴趣活动，用一句话保留看好的期待，再列出已确认的条件和仍待确认的一个细节。例如，可以期待交流顺利，同时还不知道场地开放时间。检查这个细节是为了安排活动，不是为了抵消乐观。若涉及其他人，另问他们是否愿意参加；自己的期待不能替他们承诺。事实有变化时，可以修改具体安排，而无需维护某个分区标签。
paragraphs.en: Keep one sentence describing your favourable expectation for the interest activity, then list confirmed conditions and one unchecked detail. You might expect a good exchange while not yet knowing the venue’s opening time. Checking that detail serves the arrangement rather than compensating for optimism. Ask other people separately whether they want to join; your expectation cannot commit them. Changed facts may call for a different arrangement without defending a reading-region label.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设你觉得活动大概会顺利，有哪一项条件仍值得确认，别人又有哪些选择？”先交换具体看法，不需要比较谁更乐观；同一个人也可能对不同事情有不同期待。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If you expected an activity to go reasonably well, which condition would still need confirming, and which choices would remain for others?” Exchange specific views without comparing who is more optimistic. The same person may hold different expectations about different events.

title.zh: 把希望、承诺与实际结果分开
title.en: Separate hope, commitment and the actual outcome

paragraphs.zh: 回看上面的已结束安排，分别记下当时希望怎样、自己实际答应了什么，以及后来发生了什么。没有记录的部分可以未知。一次结果可能符合期待，也可能受未预料的条件影响；两种情况都不能反推整个答卷是否准确。若以后表达期待，可以加一句仍待确认的条件，并给对方保留不同看法。这个复盘帮助说清一件事，不要求降低希望或持续保持高分。
paragraphs.en: Revisit the completed arrangement by separating what you hoped for, what you actually committed to and what happened. Leave undocumented details unknown. An outcome may match the expectation or depend on unforeseen conditions; neither establishes the accuracy of the whole questionnaire. In a future conversation, you can name a condition still needing confirmation and leave room for another view. This clarifies one event without requiring less hope or a sustained high total.

paragraphs.zh: 可以问：“假设你很期待一场活动，会怎样说明这份期待，同时不替别人保证结果？”先交换具体看法，不需要比较谁更乐观；同一个人也可能对不同事情有不同期待。
paragraphs.en: Ask: “If you were looking forward to an activity, how would you express that hope without guaranteeing the outcome for somebody else?” Exchange specific views without comparing who is more optimistic. The same person may hold different expectations about different events.
